_doc: OEM keycap profile: the sculpted profile on most prebuilt keyboards. Each row has its own height and top tilt; rows count from the top (R1, the number row) to R4 (the bottom two rows). Tilt is degrees, positive raising the top's front edge, about the top's centre. The values are KeyV2's (rsheldiii/KeyV2, src/key_profiles/oem.scad), a keycap library made for 3D printing; OEM varies a little between makers. kind as in x1c.json.
name: oem

r1_height.rule: Row 1 (number row) height at the top's centre

r4_height.source: KeyV2 oem.scad; modern boards use the row 4 profile on both bottom rows (https://deskthority.net/wiki/Keyboard_profile)

top_narrower.rule: The top is this much narrower than the base

top_shorter.rule: The top is this much shorter, front to back, than the base

top_skew.rule: The top sits this far back from the base's centre

dish.rule: Cylindrical dish depth: the top curves side to side, straight front to back
